title: Making the Sam Jones String Quartet album for East Wind
summary: He insists on a string quartet, Cedar writes four arrangements, and they record in Tokyo; later Japan tours continue.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And they also have a record company called East Wind. So we was eating breakfast one morning in the hotel lobby, getting ready to go out, getting ready to go to another town, so he saying, how would you like to make a record for us, for East Wind?

So I said well, I say, you know, I say 'it's all right but uh,' I say, 'but I'd like to make a record with some strings, string quartet.' He said oh man, he said 'there's no Japanese, Japanese can swing,' he's a Japanese telling me about the Japanese string players can't swing. I said 'I don't want them to swing, man. We do the swinging. All I want them to do is play what they see, play a part.'
